doc.title: Bill Allred interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 24, 2017

title: Family move to Orlando and the Disney big band
summary: He talks about the family's mixed feelings on the move and the variety of work with the 20-piece Disney band.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: No, what did your family think about the whole thing?

Mixed feelings. At the present time up in Illinois, see I had gotten out of the Navy and my music background in the Navy really didn’t do me a hell of a lot of good. I mean I was jobbing around the area which is, nothing going on. Dances and playing at the Elks and a couple of clubs that were decent. But yeah, there was, and it later cost me a wife. And bless her heart, she got thrust into the entertainment business which I don’t think she was quite ready for. But anyway the kids loved it. I mean my daughter ended up working at Disney selling balloons. My son got on the music staff pretty much as soon as he could graduate from high school. So that was good. And we had the 20-piece big band and we could play anything. We went back to shows, we played all the Disney stuff, all the movie music, with a 20-piece group you can do that. You’ve got eight reeds. So that was good. The nice thing about it, we had such a wide variety of stuff that you did. Well this is really interesting, probably more about Disney —
